raw_response:
I am 60 years old, and I have worked these 6 mu in Quzhou County for 40 years. With six people under my roof and only this small plot of land, I cannot afford to let any season go to waste. My schooling taught me to read the extension bulletlets and understand fertilizer labels, so I do not farm by guesswork anymore. 

This year, I will keep my main cabbage-maize-cabbage rotation on 4 mu because it is the most reliable way to turn our Hebei soil and climate into cash. Spring cabbage comes first. I will buy hybrid F1 cabbage seed from the county station, rotary till the beds after winter, and lay down a solid base of manure plus chemical fertilizer. Cabbage is a heavy feeder, so I will give it about 25 kg of nitrogen per mu, along with phosphorus and potassium. I will irrigate five times from my well because spring rains are too unpredictable to risk the heads cracking. As soon as the spring cabbage is out in early June, I will sow summer maize with no-tillage or minimal tillage to save time and soil moisture. I will use a 90-day hybrid maize so I can harvest it by late August and slip the autumn cabbage transplants in immediately after. The autumn cabbage often fetches the best price at the winter market, so I treat it with the same care as the spring crop.

On the remaining 2 mu, I will plant 0.8 mu of chili, 0.6 mu of kidney bean, and 0.6 mu of spinach. The chili peppers sell well in Handan city, but they need careful spraying against aphids and mites—about five times this season. The kidney beans give us good protein and fix a little nitrogen in the soil, and spinach is a quick cash crop in early spring. I know electricity for the well pump is expensive, so I will irrigate only when the soil truly needs it, but I will not let the crops wilt during heading or grain-fill. This is the system that has fed my family for decades, and this is what I will do.
